mainTopic: The end of the רב כהנא story; paying for informing; saving yourself with another's property and רבה's rule of the רודף; and a robber's duty for a flooded field.
overview: This amud finishes the story of רב כהנא. A serpent blocks his burial cave until רבי יוחנן humbly calls himself the student. רבי יוחנן then brings רב כהנא back to life, and רב כהנא answers all of his questions. The גמרא then rules on a man who showed רבי אבא's silk to others: judges who hold of גרמי make him pay, based on our משנה about a field shown to thugs. Next come three cases where אביי objects that a person 'saved himself with his friend's money': a silver cup given to thieves, a purse of פדיון שבויים money, and a donkey pushed off a sinking ferry. Each one ends with a special reason for the exemption. רבה's three-part rule about damage during a chase shows when a רודף, a נרדף, or a rescuer must pay. A new משנה rules that a robber may return a flooded field as it is. The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר and the חכמים disagree because they read the פסוקים by different methods, ריבוי ומיעוט versus כלל ופרט. It then asks about their parallel argument over a stolen cow, and רב פפא begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The serpent at the cave and רב כהנא brought back to life
steps.stepSummary: A serpent blocks רב כהנא's burial cave. It opens only when רבי יוחנן calls himself the student. רבי יוחנן then prays and revives רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A serpent was wrapped around the cave. רבי יוחנן said to it: 'Serpent, serpent, open your mouth and let the teacher come in to the student.' It did not open. He said: 'Let a friend come in to his friend.' It still did not open. He said: 'Let the student come in to the teacher.' Then it opened for him. He prayed for mercy and brought רב כהנא back to life.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבי יוחנן reaches רב כהנא's burial cave, but a serpent blocks the way until רבי יוחנן humbly admits that רב כהנא is his teacher. Then he prays and revives רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three requests climb down in rank: first רבי יוחנן calls himself the teacher, then an equal, and finally the student. The serpent opens only at the third request, which shows that רב כהנא really was greater. Humility is what opens the door, both in the cave and in the relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: He stood him up, here meaning he brought him back to life

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'הָרַב אֵצֶל תַּלְמִיד' as רבי יוחנן calling רב כהנא the teacher. In the first request רבי יוחנן calls HIMSELF the teacher. Only in the third request does he call himself the student, and that is the one that works.

phrases.english: A serpent was wrapped around it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the cave where רב כהנא was buried.

phrases.english: He (רבי יוחנן) said to it: 'Serpent, serpent,
open your mouth

phrases.aramaic: וְיִכָּנֵס הָרַב אֵצֶל תַּלְמִיד״, וְלָא פְּתַח.
phrases.english: and let the teacher come in to the student.' But it did not open.
'Let a friend come in to his friend.' But it did not open.
'Let the student come in to the teacher.' Then it opened for him.
He prayed for mercy and brought him back to life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב כהנא and רבי יוחנן from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The serpent lets רבי יוחנן in only once he calls himself רב כהנא's student. After that he revives רב כהנא through prayer.

steps.title: The apology, the invitation, and רב כהנא's condition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן apologizes and invites רב כהנא back. רב כהנא will come only if he won't die again, and the גמרא notes that his destined time has already passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: 'If I had known that this is the Master's way, I would not have been upset. Now let the Master come with us.' רב כהנא said: 'If you can pray that I will not die again, I will go. If not, I will not go.' The גמרא comments: since his time had passed, it had passed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן apologizes for his earlier hurt feelings and asks רב כהנא to return with him. רב כהנא puts a condition on returning, and the גמרא adds a short comment about his fated time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן admits he misjudged רב כהנא earlier. רב כהנא does not want to come back only to risk dying again. The גמרא's closing words, 'הואיל וחליף שעתא חליף', tell us that his set time of death had already passed, so he was in no danger of dying again from that decree.

keyTerms.meaning: I was upset, my feelings were hurt
Let the Master come with us
That I will not die again
Since the hour passed, it has passed

phrases.english: He (רבי יוחנן) said to him:
'If I had known
that this is the Master's way,
phrases.notes: He means how רב כהנא looked earlier in the story, which רבי יוחנן had taken the wrong way.

phrases.english: I would not have been upset.
Now let the Master come with us.'
He (רב כהנא) said to him: 'If you are able to pray for mercy
that I will not die again, I will go.
And if not, I will not go.'
Since the hour passed, it has passed.
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own comment: the time set for his death was already over, so it would not come back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוָה יָדַעְנָא דְּדַרְכֵּיהּ דְּמָר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב כהנא is alive again, the two speak, and the story moves toward his return.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא agrees to return only if he will not die again. The גמרא notes that his destined time had passed.

steps.title: רב כהנא answers every question, and the meaning of רבי יוחנן's saying
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן fully revives רב כהנא, who answers all his doubts. This explains רבי יוחנן's saying that the greatness he thought belonged to his own scholars really belongs to the scholars of בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He woke him up fully and stood him up. He asked him every doubt he had, and רב כהנא answered them all for him. This is what רבי יוחנן meant when he said: 'I said it was yours, but it is theirs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רב כהנא, now fully alive, solves all of רבי יוחנן's questions, and the גמרא ties this to a well-known saying of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא came from בבל, and his mastery proves that the scholars of בבל were greater than רבי יוחנן had assumed. 'היינו דאמר' tells us this story is the background to רבי יוחנן's saying. It closes the whole story with its lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what [so-and-so] meant when he said
I said it was yours, but it is theirs

steps.whatToRemember: The story of רב כהנא ends with its lesson: a scholar from בבל answered all of רבי יוחנן's questions, so רבי יוחנן admitted that the greater Torah strength was in בבל.

phrases.english: He woke him up and stood him up.
He asked him every doubt that he had,
and he (רב כהנא) resolved them for him.
This is what רבי יוחנן meant when he said:
'I said it was yours, but it is theirs.'
phrases.notes: "Yours" means the scholars of ארץ ישראל; "theirs" means the scholars of בבל, where רב כהנא came from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the revival story and draws its lesson.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב כהנא's ability to answer every doubt is the source of רבי יוחנן's saying that the scholars of בבל are the greater ones.

steps.title: A new case: the man who showed רבי אבא's silk
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins: a man showed רבי אבא's silk to others, and רבי אבהו, רבי חנינא בר פפי and רבי יצחק נפחא sit down to judge, with רבי אילעא sitting with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain man who showed רבי אבא's silk. רבי אבהו, רבי חנינא בר פפי and רבי יצחק נפחא sat to judge the case, and רבי אילעא sat with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the רב כהנא story and opens a new case about a מוסר who showed another person's property. This line only sets the scene; the discussion of the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This brings the סוגיא back to its main subject, informing on someone's property. The man pointed out רבי אבא's silk, and it was taken. Whether the informer must pay is discussed in the next steps; here we only meet the judges.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case returns the סוגיא from אגדה back to the practical laws of a מוסר and his duty to pay.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who showed
רבי אבא's silk.
phrases.notes: He showed it to non-Jews, who then took it, which is why it is a case of informing.

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵיב רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפִּי
phrases.english: רבי אבהו and רבי חנינא בר פפי sat
and רבי יצחק נפחא,
and רבי אילעא sat next to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, unrelated to רב כהנא, that returns to the topic of informers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a man informed on רבי אבא's silk, and a court of אמוראים sits to decide it.

steps.title: The judges try to prove liability from a judge who rules wrongly
steps.stepSummary: The judges want to make the man who showed the silk pay. Their proof is the משנה that says a judge who rules wrongly must pay from his own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought to make him pay, based on the משנה: if a judge decided a case and let the guilty party go, or made the innocent party pay, or called something pure impure, or impure pure, his ruling stands and he pays from his own pocket.
steps.whatsHappening: The three judges look for a source that would make the man who showed רבי אבא's silk pay for the loss. They bring a משנה about a judge who makes a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge in the משנה caused a loss only by speaking, yet he has to pay. So the judges reason that the man who only pointed out the silk with words should also have to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: They thought to make him liable
What he did stays done (the ruling is not reversed)
And he pays from his own pocket

phrases.english: They thought to make him liable
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the man who showed רבי אבא's silk to others, from step 4.

phrases.english: from what we learned in a משנה:
If one judged a case

phrases.aramaic: זִיכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּיב וְחִיֵּיב אֶת הַזַּכַּאי,
phrases.english: and acquitted the liable one, or made the innocent one liable,

phrases.aramaic: טִימֵּא אֶת הַטָּהוֹר וְטִיהֵר אֶת הַטָּמֵא –
phrases.english: or declared the pure impure, or the impure pure,
what he did is done,
and he must pay from his house.
phrases.notes: 'From his house' means out of his own money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The judges seated in step 4 now begin their ruling and offer a source for it.
steps.raayaObject: That the man who showed the silk must pay for the loss
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the judge who erred and pays from his own pocket

steps.title: The judge only pays when he handled the money himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא quotes רב: the judge in that משנה pays only when he physically took the money and handed it over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said to them: this is what רב said. That משנה is talking about a judge who took the money and handed it over with his own hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא knocks down the judges' proof. The judge in the משנה did more than speak, because he physically moved the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the judge's payment comes from a physical act, the משנה no longer proves anything about someone who caused a loss only with words. So the case of the silk is left without a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Took and gave with his own hand (physically moved the money)

phrases.english: רבי אילעא said to them:
This is what רב said:
And that is only where he took and gave by hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי אִילְעָא, הָכִי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the judge's משנה only, not the question of whether the man owes money
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The judge in the משנה acted physically, while the man who showed the silk only spoke.

steps.title: The judges send רבי אבא to judges who rule on indirect damage
steps.stepSummary: Left without a proof, the judges send רבי אבא to רבי שמעון בן אליקים and רבי אלעזר בן פדת, who make people pay for indirect damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: go to רבי שמעון בן אליקים and רבי אלעזר בן פדת, who make people pay for damage they cause indirectly.
steps.whatsHappening: The judges will not rule on the case themselves, so they send רבי אבא elsewhere. This sets up the next step, where the case is decided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These judges do not hold someone liable for גרמי (indirect damage). Other judges do, so the case goes to them.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of indirect damage, which makes a person pay for a loss he caused indirectly

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי אבא, the owner of the silk.

phrases.aramaic: זִיל לְגַבֵּי דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים
phrases.english: Go to רבי שמעון בן אליקים
and רבי אלעזר בן פדת,
who judge the law of indirect damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof fails, the judges step back and send the case to other judges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for indirect damage depends on which judges hold the view of גרמי.

steps.title: The second judges make the man pay, based on the field shown to thugs
steps.stepSummary: The second judges make the man pay, based on the משנה that a robber whose fault caused a field to be seized must supply another field. That משנה was explained as talking about someone who showed the field to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to them, and they made him pay based on our משנה: if the field was seized because of the robber, he must supply another field. And we explained that משנה as talking about someone who only pointed the field out.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: רבי אבא wins. The judges use a משנה from this פרק to make the man who showed the silk pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pointing out a field is like pointing out silk. Both cause a loss only by showing it to others. Since the משנה makes the one who pointed liable, the man who showed the silk is liable too.

keyTerms.meaning: To supply him with a different field

steps.whatToRemember: Showing someone's property to people who then take it can make you pay, according to the judges who hold the view of גרמי.

phrases.english: He went to them,
and they made him liable from our משנה:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה earlier in this פרק about a stolen field that thugs then seized.

phrases.english: If it was because of the robber,
he must supply him with another field;
and we explained it as where he merely pointed it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The judges named in step 7 decide the case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The man who showed the silk must pay, just like someone who points out a field that thugs then seize.

steps.title: A שומר gives a deposited silver cup to thieves, and רבה exempts him
steps.stepSummary: A new story: thieves come to a שומר holding a silver cup, and he hands it to them. רבה rules that he does not have to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man was given a silver cup to look after. Thieves came at him, and he took the cup and gave it to them. He came before רבה, who said he does not have to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new case about a שומר who gave away a deposit to thieves. רבה's ruling is the starting point that the next steps will discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether handing over someone else's item under threat counts as the שומר's own act of damage. רבה treats it as something the שומר could not help, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Was given to him to look after

phrases.english: There was a certain man
who had a silver cup deposited with him.
Thieves came up against him,
and he took it and gave it to them.
He came before רבה, and he exempted him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲוָה מִפְּקִיד לֵיהּ כָּסָא דְכַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on a related theme: causing loss to someone else's property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: a שומר who hands a deposit to thieves is exempt.

steps.title: אביי objects that the שומר saved himself with someone else's money
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: the שומר used someone else's property to protect himself, so he should pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: this man is saving himself with his friend's money!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's ruling. He says this is a well-known case of a person who protects himself by using up someone else's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that you may not save yourself at your friend's expense, and if you do, you must pay. אביי says giving the cup to the thieves is exactly that, so רבה's exemption seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Saves himself with his friend's money, which makes him liable

phrases.english: אביי said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ בְּמָמוֹן חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא!
phrases.english: This one is saving himself with his friend's money!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ בְּמָמוֹן חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's exemption from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the שומר is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who saves himself with another person's money must pay, and that is what this שומר did.

steps.title: רב אשי: it depends on whether the שומר is wealthy
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that we check who the thieves came for. If the שומר is rich, they came for him, and he must pay. If not, they came for the cup, and he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: we look. If the man is wealthy, the thieves came for his things. If not, they came for the silver.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers אביי's objection by splitting the case in two, based on the שומר's wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the thieves came for the שומר's own money, handing over the cup protected him at the owner's expense, so he pays. If they came for the cup anyway, the owner's loss would have happened no matter what, so the שומר did not save himself with another's money and is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: With his own property in mind

steps.whatToRemember: A שומר who hands a deposit to thieves pays only if they really came for his own wealth. If they came for the deposit itself, he is exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the outcomes: the rich שומר is the one who pays, because the thieves came for him and he used the cup to protect himself.

phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said:
We look:
If he is a wealthy man,
they came with his own property in mind,
and if not, they came for the silver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by limiting רבה's exemption.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the case based on who the thieves were really after
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either the שומר is always exempt (רבה) or he is always liable for saving himself with another's money (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: A wealthy שומר pays because the thieves came for him. A שומר who is not wealthy is exempt because they came for the cup.

steps.title: The man who handed over the purse for redeeming captives
steps.stepSummary: A man held a purse of פדיון שבויים money. Thieves attacked, he gave them the purse, and רבא exempted him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who was holding a purse of money collected for redeeming captives. Thieves came at him, and he took the purse and gave it to them. The case came before רבא, and he ruled the man does not have to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. A שומר gave away charity money meant for captives to save himself from thieves, and רבא said he does not have to pay it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This looks like the earlier silver cup case, but here the money belongs to a fund for freeing captives. The ruling is that he does not pay, and the reason will come out in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeeming captives, buying back people who were kidnapped
It was left with him for safekeeping

phrases.english: There was a certain man who had deposited with him
a purse of money for redeeming captives.
Thieves came upon him,
he took it and gave it to them.
The case came before רבא, and he exempted him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme as the silver cup case: a שומר who gives up deposited property to escape thieves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר who gave the captives' purse to thieves does not have to pay.

steps.title: אביי objects that he saved himself with others' money
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues the man should pay, since he used other people's money to save himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But this man is saving himself with someone else's money!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the ruling. A person is not allowed to save himself by giving away someone else's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same rule אביי used against the silver cup ruling. The money was not his, and he used it to protect himself, so he should have to pay it back.

keyTerms.meaning: With his friend's money or property

phrases.english: אביי said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ בְּמָמוֹן חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא!
phrases.english: But he is saving himself with his friend's money!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא מַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ בְּמָמוֹן חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the exemption given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the man does not have to pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is forbidden to save yourself with another person's property, so using the captives' money to escape the thieves should make him pay.

steps.title: There is no greater redemption of captives than this
steps.stepSummary: The money was meant to save people from captors, and here it saved this man from the thieves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is no greater redemption of captives than this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the money was actually used for exactly what it was collected for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fund exists to rescue people from dangerous captors. When the man handed it over to save himself from the thieves, he was himself being rescued. So he did not take the money for his own private use. It went to its proper purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: You have no..., there is nothing

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ פִּדְיוֹן שְׁבוּיִים גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה.
phrases.english: You have no greater redemption of captives than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לְךָ פִּדְיוֹן שְׁבוּיִים גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the money was used for its intended purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man used other people's money to save himself, so he should pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saving a person from thieves is itself פדיון שבויים, so the money went where it was meant to go and he is exempt.

steps.title: The donkey that was about to sink the ferry
steps.stepSummary: A man brought his donkey onto a ferry early. The boat began to sink, another man pushed the donkey into the river, and רבה exempted him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man hurried and brought his donkey onto a ferry before the other people boarded. The ferry was about to sink. Another man came, pushed the first man's donkey into the river, and it drowned. The case came before רבה, and he ruled the pusher does not have to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. Someone destroyed another person's donkey to save the boat, and רבה said he does not pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a person did not just hand over property. He actively destroyed it to save himself and others. Even so, רבה exempts him, which sets up another challenge from אביי.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who hurried
and brought his donkey up onto the ferry,
before the people boarded the ferry.
It was about to sink,
a certain man came,
pushed the donkey of that first man
and threw it into the river, and it drowned.
The case came before רבה, and he exempted him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַקְדֵּים וְאַסֵּיק חֲמָרָא לְמַבָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme: damaging someone else's property to escape danger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man who pushed the donkey overboard to save the ferry does not have to pay.

steps.title: אביי objects again: he saved himself with the donkey
steps.stepSummary: אביי repeats his objection: the pusher saved himself by destroying someone else's donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But this man is saving himself with someone else's property!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה with the same rule as before. You may not save yourself by destroying your friend's things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pusher was on the boat too, so drowning the donkey saved his own life. Under the rule against saving yourself with your friend's money, he should have to pay for the donkey.

phrases.english: אביי said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ בְּמָמוֹן חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא!
phrases.english: But he is saving himself with his friend's property!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא מַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ בְּמָמוֹן חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the exemption given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the man who drowned the donkey does not have to pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He destroyed another person's property to save himself, which is forbidden, so he should pay.

steps.title: The donkey's owner was a pursuer from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the donkey's owner was a רודף, because his donkey put everyone's life in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This donkey's owner was a pursuer from the very start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains that the donkey's owner counts as a רודף, someone who puts other people's lives at risk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By loading his donkey early and making the boat start to sink, the owner was endangering everyone on board. A רודף's property may be destroyed to stop the danger. So this is not a case of using an innocent person's money to save yourself.

keyTerms.meaning: A pursuer, someone putting another person's life in danger

steps.confusionAlert: The owner did not mean to hurt anyone, and he is not punished. He is called a רודף only because his donkey was the thing putting lives in danger, so it was allowed to destroy it.

phrases.english: He said to him: This one
phrases.notes: "This one" means the owner of the donkey.

phrases.english: was a pursuer from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the owner of the property is a רודף
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The donkey belonged to an innocent person, so destroying it means saving yourself with another's property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The donkey's owner was a רודף, and a רודף's property may be destroyed to stop the danger, so there is no payment.

steps.title: רבה's rule: a pursuer who breaks things does not pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבה follows his own known rule. First part: a רודף who breaks anyone's vessels during the chase is exempt, because he is liable with his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה follows his own reasoning, as רבה said: A pursuer who was chasing his friend to kill him and broke vessels, whether they belonged to the pursued person or to anyone else, is exempt, because he is liable with his life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבה's general teaching about a רודף to show his ruling about the donkey fits his usual view. This first part sets up the part that really matters for the donkey case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he is chasing someone to kill him, the רודף deserves to die. When a person becomes liable for death and money damage at the same moment, he does not pay the money. So whatever he breaks during the chase, no matter whose it is, he does not pay for.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his other rulings
He is liable with his life

phrases.english: רבה follows his own reasoning,
as רבה said:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹדֵף שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחַר חֲבֵירוֹ לְהוֹרְגוֹ,
phrases.english: A pursuer who was chasing his friend to kill him,
and he broke vessels,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁל נִרְדָּף בֵּין שֶׁל כָּל אָדָם – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: whether of the pursued one or of anyone else, is exempt,
because he is liable with his life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבה's answer in step 17 matches his general teaching about a רודף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רודף who breaks anyone's vessels during the chase is exempt, because he is liable with his life.

steps.title: The pursued may break the pursuer's things, but must pay for others'
steps.stepSummary: Second part of רבה's rule: a נרדף who breaks the רודף's vessels is exempt, but if he breaks anyone else's he must pay, because you may not save yourself with your friend's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a pursued person who broke the pursuer's vessels is exempt, so that the pursuer's property should not be more precious to him than his body. But if he broke anyone else's vessels, he must pay, because it is forbidden to save yourself with your friend's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבה's rule. This part explains both the donkey case and אביי's objection: the רודף's things may be destroyed, but innocent people's things may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you may even kill the רודף to stop him, you may certainly destroy his property. But a bystander did nothing wrong, so breaking his things to save yourself means you must pay. In the ferry, the donkey's owner was the רודף, which is why the pusher did not pay.
steps.whatToRemember: A person may destroy the property of the one endangering him, but he must pay for anyone else's property he damages to save himself. That is why the donkey pusher was exempt: the donkey's owner was the רודף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains every story in this section: the rule against saving yourself with your friend's money stays in force, and each exemption came from a special reason in that case.

phrases.aramaic: וְנִרְדָּף שֶׁשִּׁיבֵּר אֶת הַכֵּלִים שֶׁל רוֹדֵף – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: And a pursued person who broke the pursuer's vessels is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא מָמוֹנוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ.
phrases.english: so that his property should not be dearer to him than his body.
But if they belonged to anyone else, he is liable,
because it is forbidden to save oneself with one's friend's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִרְדָּף שֶׁשִּׁיבֵּר אֶת הַכֵּלִים שֶׁל רוֹדֵף – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבה's teaching from step 18 and gives the rule that supports his answer in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A נרדף is exempt for breaking the רודף's property but must pay for breaking anyone else's, since saving yourself with your friend's property is forbidden.

steps.title: A rescuer who breaks things while chasing an attacker is exempt
steps.stepSummary: Third part of רבה's rule: someone chasing a רודף to save the victim does not pay for anything he breaks, whether it belongs to the attacker or to anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person chases after a רודף to save the victim and breaks vessels along the way, he is exempt, whether the vessels belonged to the one he is chasing or to any other person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third and last part of רבה's rule about damage during a chase. This part is about the rescuer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the victim may not save himself with other people's property. Here the rescuer gets more protection than the victim: he is exempt even for an outsider's vessels. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: Any person, meaning an outsider not involved in the chase

steps.confusionAlert: In this line, the word נרדף does not mean the victim. It means the person the rescuer is chasing, who is the attacker himself.

phrases.english: And a pursuer who was chasing
after a pursuer in order to save,
and he broke vessels,
whether those of the pursued one
phrases.notes: Here the "pursued one" is the attacker, since the rescuer is the one chasing him.

phrases.english: or those of any person, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרוֹדֵף שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחַר רוֹדֵף לְהַצִּיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's three-part rule after the cases of the רודף (step 18) and the נרדף (step 19).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rescuer chasing a רודף is exempt for any vessels he breaks, whether they belong to the attacker or to anyone else.

steps.title: Why the rescuer is exempt: so people will still save others
steps.stepSummary: The rescuer's exemption is not the strict law. It is a rule made so that people will not hold back from saving lives.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not the strict law. But if you do not say this, no one will ever save his friend from a רודף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason for the rescuer's exemption and closes the section on רבה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the strict law, the rescuer should pay just like the victim does, since he also used someone else's property. The חכמים exempted him anyway. If rescuers had to pay for damage, they would be afraid to help.

keyTerms.meaning: If you do not say so (if we do not make this rule)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule has three parts. The רודף never pays, since he is liable with his life. The victim pays for anyone's property except the רודף's. The rescuer never pays, because of a rule of the חכמים that encourages saving lives.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the הלכה sometimes sets aside strict monetary law so that people will not hold back from saving a life.

phrases.english: And this is not from the strict law,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם אִי אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן –
phrases.english: but rather, if you do not say so,
you will have no person who saves
his friend from the pursuer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא מִן הַדִּין, אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם אִי אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the exemption stated in step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rescuer's exemption is a rule of the חכמים, made so that people will be willing to save lives.

steps.title: משנה: a stolen field flooded by a river
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a river floods a stolen field, the robber may tell the owner, "Here is yours in front of you."
steps.simpleTranslation: If a river flooded the stolen field, the robber says to the owner: "Here is yours, in front of you."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. If a stolen field is ruined by a flood, the robber just gives back the land as it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land cannot really be taken away. It stays the owner's and stays in its place. So damage from a flood is not counted as the robber's loss, and he does not have to pay for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A river flooded it (washed it away)
Here is yours in front of you

phrases.english: Mishnah
If a river flooded it,
phrases.notes: "It" means a field that was stolen.

phrases.english: he says to him: "Here is yours before you."

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁטָפָהּ נָהָר, אוֹמֵר לוֹ: הֲרֵי שֶׁלְּךָ לְפָנֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the רודף discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A robber whose stolen field was flooded may return it as it is and owes nothing more.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי אלעזר and the חכמים disagree about the flooded field
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the robber must give a different field. The חכמים say he may return the flooded one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: if someone steals a field and a river floods it, he must give the owner a different field. This is the view of רבי אלעזר. The חכמים say he tells the owner, "Here is yours in front of you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the ruling of the משנה is actually under debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה follows the חכמים. רבי אלעזר treats a stolen field like any stolen object: once it is ruined while in the robber's hands, the robber must make it up. That is why he must give a replacement field.

keyTerms.meaning: To provide him a different field

phrases.english: Gemara. The Sages taught:
One who robs a field from his friend
and a river flooded it,
is obligated to provide him another field,
the words of Rabbi Elazar.
And the Sages say,
he says to him: "Here is yours before you."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַגּוֹזֵל שָׂדֶה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ וּשְׁטָפָהּ נָהָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא showing that the ruling of the משנה is debated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: the robber must give a replacement field. חכמים: he returns the flooded field as it is.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the basis of the argument is between רבי אלעזר and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the debate. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know which source or principle leads each side to its view. The answer will be based on how they read the פסוקים.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the debate in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle or reading of the פסוק underlies the argument between רבי אלעזר and the חכמים.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר reads the פסוקים as an amplification, a restriction, and another amplification
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר uses the method of ריבוי ומיעוט. "And deal falsely with his neighbor" includes. "In a deposit" limits. "Anything he swore falsely about" includes again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר expounds the Torah using amplifications and restrictions. "And he deals falsely with his neighbor" includes. "In a deposit" limits. "Anything about which he swore falsely" goes back and includes again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer by showing how רבי אלעזר reads the פסוקים about one who denies and swears falsely. It lays out the pattern of the words. The next step gives the conclusion for land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the method of ריבוי ומיעוט, a general word that includes, followed by a narrow word that limits, followed by another word that includes, together include almost everything. This is how רבי אלעזר will show that land is also covered by the robber's duty to repay.

keyTerms.meaning: Amplifications and restrictions, a method of reading the Torah's wording
And he deals falsely with his neighbor
A deposit, an object left with someone for safekeeping
It went back and included again

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the method of כלל ופרט. In ריבוי ומיעוט, the final inclusion covers much more, almost everything.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar expounds amplifications and restrictions;
"And deal falsely with his neighbor": it amplified,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:21. Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: "In a deposit": it restricted,
"Anything about which he swore falsely":
it went back and amplified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 24 by showing רבי אלעזר's method of reading the פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר reads the פסוקים by ריבוי ומיעוט: an inclusion, then a limitation, then another inclusion. This sets up his conclusion that land is included in the robber's duty to repay.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's reading includes everything except documents
steps.stepSummary: Because the פסוק includes, then limits, then includes again, it includes everything. The only thing left out is documents, so land is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah included, then limited, then included again. That means it included everything. What did it include? All things. What did it leave out? Documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining how רבי אלעזר reads the פסוקים. It tells us what is included and what is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the method of ריבוי ומיעוט, the second 'including' word is very strong. It brings back almost everything, and the 'limiting' word only removes one small thing. Here only שטרות are removed, so land stays included. That is why, for רבי אלעזר, a robber of land is responsible for it and must give a different field.

keyTerms.meaning: It included, meaning the words of the פסוק make the law wider
It limited, meaning the words leave something out

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains רבי אלעזר's ruling in the ברייתא. Since land is included in the robber's duty to return or pay, a flooded field must be replaced.

phrases.english: It included, and limited, and included again:
it included everything.
And what did it include?
It included all things.
And what did it leave out?
It left out documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ריבוי ומיעוט reading that began in step 25 and gives its result.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר reads the פסוקים as ריבוי ומיעוט ריבוי, which includes everything except שטרות. So land is included.

steps.title: The חכמים read the same פסוקים as general-detail-general
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים read the same words using the method of כלל ופרט. This method includes only things similar to the detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים use the method of general statements and details. 'And deal falsely' is a general statement. 'In a deposit' is a detail. 'Or anything' goes back and makes a general statement again. When there is a general statement, a detail, and another general statement, you include only things similar to the detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the other side of the argument. It shows how the חכמים read the very same פסוקים in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the same three phrases רבי אלעזר used, but the חכמים use a different method. In כלל ופרט וכלל, the detail controls the meaning. Only things that are like the detail are included. The next step will explain what the detail (a deposit) is like.

keyTerms.meaning: They explain or interpret the פסוק
A general statement, then a detail, then another general statement
A deposit, something left with another person to watch

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two methods! They use the same three phrases but give opposite results. ריבוי ומיעוט includes almost everything. כלל ופרט וכלל includes only things similar to the detail. That is the whole basis of the argument.

phrases.english: And the חכמים interpret using general statements and details.
"And deal falsely" is a general statement,
"in a deposit" is a detail,
"or anything": it went back and made a general statement again.
A general statement, a detail, and a general statement:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְעֵין הַפְּרָט;
phrases.english: you may include only things similar to the detail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים's method for the same פסוקים, as the other half of the answer to the question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים read the פסוקים as כלל ופרט וכלל, so only things similar to the detail (a deposit) are included.

steps.title: Only movable things with value of their own are included, so land is left out
steps.stepSummary: A deposit can be moved and is worth money in itself. So land, slaves, and documents are all left out according to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The detail, a deposit, is something that can be moved and is worth money in itself. So too, the law includes anything that can be moved and is worth money in itself. Land is left out, because it cannot be moved. Slaves are left out, because the Torah compares them to land. Documents are left out, because even though they can be moved, they are not worth money in themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what 'similar to the detail' means. Then it lists what is left out, and land is one of those things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deposit has two features: it can be moved, and the item itself is worth money. Land fails the first test. Documents fail the second test, because the paper only proves a debt. Slaves are treated like land. Since land is not included in the robber's duty to pay, the robber can simply return the flooded field, as the חכמים say.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable, something that can be carried from place to place
The item itself is worth money
They were compared, meaning the Torah treats them like something else

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is about how to read the פסוקים. רבי אלעזר uses ריבוי ומיעוט, so land is included and the robber must give a different field. The חכמים use כלל ופרט וכלל, so only movable things worth money in themselves are included. Land is left out, so the robber may say "Here is yours in front of you."

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַפְּרָט – דָּבָר הַמִּיטַּלְטֵל וְגוּפוֹ מָמוֹן,
phrases.english: Just as the detail is something movable that is worth money in itself,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל דָּבָר הַמִּיטַּלְטֵל וְגוּפוֹ מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: so too, anything that is movable and worth money in itself is included.
Land is left out, because it is not movable.
Slaves are left out, because they are compared to land.

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאוּ שְׁטָרוֹת – שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּטַּלְטְלִין,
phrases.english: Documents are left out, because even though they are movable,
they are not worth money in themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה הַפְּרָט – דָּבָר הַמִּיטַּלְטֵל וְגוּפוֹ מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the כלל ופרט וכלל rule from step 27 to define the category and list what is left out.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the חכמים, only movable things worth money in themselves are included. Land is left out, which explains why the robber may return the flooded field as it is.

steps.title: A stolen cow swept away by a river
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא where רבי אלעזר and the חכמים argue about a stolen cow swept away by a river. It asks what their argument could be about, since a cow fits even the חכמים' narrow reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא: if someone stole a cow and a river washed it away, רבי אלעזר says he must give the owner a cow. The חכמים say he can tell the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you.' What is their argument about there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where the same two sides argue about a cow, not land. It asks what the argument could be based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28 we learned the חכמים only include things like a deposit: movable and worth money in itself. A cow fits that perfectly, so the argument about the cow cannot be about ריבוי ומיעוט versus כלל ופרט. That means their argument must have some other basis.

keyTerms.meaning: And there is what was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a source that seems to conflict)
Here is yours before you (the robber gives back what he took and owes nothing more)

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds strange that the חכמים let a robber off when the cow is gone. Hold that question; רב פפא is about to explain that the case is really different from what it looks like.

phrases.english: And there is that which was taught:
One who robbed a cow
and a river washed it away
is obligated to provide him a cow,
these are the words of Rabbi Elazar.
And the Rabbis say: he says to him:
"Here is yours before you."
There, about what do they disagree?
